name: Robin Healthcare vs Freed
title: Robin Healthcare vs Freed: Hardware vs Software AI Scribe Comparison
description: Compare Robin Healthcare (hardware device) and Freed (software only) AI scribes. See differences in deployment, pricing, and target audiences.

summary.bottom_line: Robin Healthcare uses dedicated hardware (Robin Assistant device) for ambient documentation, while Freed is software-only using your existing devices. Robin is for established practices ready for infrastructure investment; Freed is for any clinician wanting to start immediately at $39-119/month.

key_differences.target_market: Robin (group practices) vs Freed (solo to enterprise)

sections.heading: Robin Healthcare vs Freed: Overview
sections.content: Robin Healthcare and Freed represent fundamentally different approaches to AI medical documentation. Robin Healthcare uses a dedicated hardware device (Robin Assistant) that sits in exam rooms to capture patient-physician conversations—appealing to practices wanting purpose-built infrastructure without relying on personal devices. Freed is software-only, working through browser extensions and mobile apps with no hardware required. Robin reports 90 minutes saved per day with 98% patient acceptance; Freed claims 70%+ documentation time reduction. The choice comes down to deployment preference and budget.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Freed has transparent public pricing: Starter ($39/mo, 40 notes), Core ($79/mo, unlimited), Premier ($119/mo, EHR push + ICD-10). Robin Healthcare does not publish pricing—it involves hardware purchase/lease plus software subscription, requiring enterprise quotes. The hardware investment means Robin likely costs more upfront but provides dedicated infrastructure. For individual clinicians, Freed is more accessible; for practices wanting consistent documentation hardware across exam rooms, Robin may justify the investment.

sections.heading: Feature Differences
sections.content: Robin's key advantage is dedicated hardware—the Robin Assistant device captures audio consistently without clinicians managing phones or laptops. This appeals to practices wanting uniform documentation infrastructure. Freed's advantages are flexibility (works on any device), telehealth support (Robin is in-person focused), immediate availability (sign up today vs. hardware deployment), and transparent pricing. Both integrate with major EHRs (Epic, Cerner, athenahealth). For telehealth-heavy practices, Freed is clearly better; for in-person ambulatory practices wanting dedicated hardware, Robin has appeal.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Choose based on your deployment preferences:

recommendations.when: You're a multi-provider ambulatory practice, want dedicated hardware in each exam room, prefer not relying on personal devices, and are ready for infrastructure investment
You're a solo practitioner or small practice, want to start immediately without hardware, do telehealth, or prefer transparent pricing you can sign up for today
You do any telehealth—Robin's hardware-based approach is designed for in-person visits while Freed works seamlessly across both

faqs.q: What is the Robin Assistant device?
faqs.a: The Robin Assistant is a dedicated hardware device that sits in exam rooms to capture patient-physician conversations. Unlike software-only AI scribes that use phone or computer microphones, Robin uses purpose-built hardware for ambient documentation.

faqs.q: Can I use Robin Healthcare for telehealth?
faqs.a: Robin Healthcare is designed primarily for in-person visits using the hardware device. It has limited telehealth support. Freed works equally well for telehealth (Zoom, Doxy.me) and in-person visits.

faqs.q: Is Robin Healthcare available for solo practitioners?
faqs.a: Robin Healthcare targets multi-provider ambulatory practices ready for infrastructure investment. Solo practitioners would likely find Freed more accessible with its transparent pricing and immediate availability without hardware deployment.

Robin reports 90 minutes saved per day; Freed reports 70%+ documentation time reduction. Both represent significant time savings. Actual results depend on specialty, documentation habits, and workflow integration.
